QF.id: XVI Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_11

question.text: Penalty on seller for delivery default in agri-commodity futures is:

answer.text: 4% of Settlement Price + replacement cost, where replacement cost uses the average of the three highest last spot prices of the five succeeding days after the commodity pay-out date if that average is higher than the Settlement Price
No penalty — delivery default is not penalized

explanation.text: The Logic: For agri-commodities, seller delivery default attracts 4% of the Settlement Price plus a replacement cost component. Replacement cost is computed as the excess of the average of the three highest last spot prices of the five succeeding days after the commodity pay-out date over the Settlement Price, only if that average is higher than the Settlement Price. The Trap: The 3% slab is for non-agri commodities, not agri. The five-succeeding-day window after the pay-out date, taking the three highest last spot prices, is the agri-specific reference — not a generic three-day average before pay-out. Note: The 4% plus replacement-cost framework is the regulator-prescribed structure, with apportionment to the SGF, the clearing corporation, and the non-defaulting buyer.
